correctness.rationale: Every difference |v_j-v_i| telescopes across positive adjacent house-value gaps. At prefix r, the cross-cut edge count equals r(N-r)-sum_i x_i(r)(n_i-x_i(r)). The within-part term has strictly decreasing marginal priorities n_i-2k-1. Choosing largest r globally maximizes the term; one common sorted priority order attains every cut maximum simultaneously. Strictly positive gaps require every such optimum, proving iff with tied-level choices. Each part contributes at most one priority per level, yielding product_w m_w! words times product_i n_i! labelled allocations. Independent brute-force direct edge-cost enumeration checked 364 instances and 408204 complete part-label words on small q=3..5, N<=8, two distinct strictly increasing valuation patterns; finite verification is corroboration only.
